Reporting rule (outline): write every proportion as a percentage to 1 decimal place and name the reference group, e.g., '40.0% of commuters'.

P(A | B) means the share of group B that is also in A: count(A and B) / count(B). The group after the bar is the reference group and denominator. Order matters; P(A | B) and P(B | A) generally differ.

blocks.setup: Practice set A Q1: 25 of 40 students commute; 10 commuters cycle.

steps.label: Choose reference group
steps.text: The question asks about commuters, so use the 25 commuters.

blocks.takeaway: Use the restricted group named by the question, not the whole class.

sections.title: T2 Two-way tables: choose the denominator

blocks.text: One shared example. Rows are commute status; columns are cycling status. Cell counts: commuters—cycle 10, do not cycle 15 (row total 25); noncommuters—cycle 5, do not cycle 20 (row total 25). Column totals: cycle 15, do not cycle 35.

blocks.setup: Read the same cell (commuters who cycle) under two different reference groups.

steps.label: Row percentage
steps.text: 10 / 25 = 40.0% of commuters cycle. Divide by the commuters row total.

steps.label: Column percentage
steps.text: 10 / 15 = 66.7% of cyclists are commuters. Divide by the cycling column total.

blocks.takeaway: First name the reference group; its row or column total is the denominator. Row percentages sum to 100% across each row; column percentages sum to 100% down each column.

blocks.prompt: Prior reviewed table item: selected a row total for a column percentage.
blocks.first_error: Used the row total even though the question specified a column percentage.
blocks.fix: For a column percentage, divide the cell by its column total; say the reference group in words.
blocks.conditions: The denominator is the total for the reference group requested.

blocks.text: Split cases by a categorical variable and compute the chosen summary (such as a mean or count) for each group. The output has one row per non-empty group, not one per original case. Compare like summaries (mean with mean, total with total). (Notes section 3; 2025 midterm Q3 illustrates row count.)
